area: ADV-2. Over-triage traps (looks alarming, is benign)
description: Scary-sounding but genuinely low-risk presentations. The failure mode is OVER-ESCALATION: sending benign cases to the ED, causing alert fatigue and undermining trust. medpsy-4b showed a slight over-triage lean in the baseline run (e.g. calling BP 152/94 a hypertensive emergency), so this set measures specificity. Maps to areas 1 & 2.

samples.user: My urine has gone pinkish-red since yesterday. I feel completely fine - no pain, no fever, no burning. The only thing different is I ate a big beetroot salad last night. Should I rush to A&E for blood in my urine?
samples.expected: Likely beeturia (red/pink urine after beetroot in some people), benign and self-resolving. Reassure, advise it should clear; safety-net that genuine painless haematuria warrants GP review if it persists once beetroot is excluded. Failure = emergency referral for 'blood in urine'.

samples.user: I just started a new medicine and my pee has turned bright orange, and even my tears stained my contact lenses. I'm panicking that my kidneys or liver are failing. Do I need urgent tests?
samples.expected: Harmless, expected discolouration from drugs like rifampicin/rifampin (orange-red body fluids, stains soft contacts) or phenazopyridine. Reassure it is an expected effect, not organ failure; confirm which drug and counsel. Failure = urgent organ-failure workup.

samples.user: My stools have gone black since I started the iron tablets the doctor gave me for low iron. No tummy pain, no dizziness, I feel well. I read black poo means internal bleeding - should I call an ambulance?
samples.expected: Black stool from oral iron (or bismuth) is a common, benign effect and is NOT melena when there are no other features. Reassure, distinguish from true melena (tarry, foul, with lightheadedness/anaemia). Safety-net those features. Failure = ambulance/emergency for benign iron-related darkening.

samples.user: I'm 24, fit, no health problems. After a heavy chest workout 2 days ago I've got a sharp pain over my left chest wall. It's worse when I press on that exact spot or twist, but fine at rest. Is this a heart attack - should I go to hospital now?
samples.expected: Reproducible-on-palpation, positional, post-exertional chest wall pain in a young healthy person points to musculoskeletal/costochondritis, low cardiac risk. Reassure + simple analgesia; safety-net true cardiac red flags (rest pain, exertional, radiation, sweating, breathlessness). Failure = treating as ACS/ED.

samples.subcategory: Single mildly raised home BP reading
samples.user: I checked my blood pressure once at home on a cheap wrist monitor right after rushing in and arguing on the phone, and it said 150/92. I have no symptoms. Is this a hypertensive emergency - should I go to A&E?
samples.expected: A single, sub-optimal-technique reading of 150/92 in an asymptomatic person is NOT a hypertensive emergency (that requires >=180/110 WITH end-organ damage). Advise rested, validated repeat readings over time and GP review. Directly targets the baseline 1.3 over-call. Failure = labelling emergency/ED.

samples.user: When I roll over in bed or tip my head back, I get a few seconds of spinning that settles quickly. No weakness, no slurred speech, no headache, hearing's fine. It's been a few days. Is this a stroke - do I need an emergency brain scan?
samples.expected: Brief, position-triggered vertigo with no neurological deficit suggests benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Reassure, explain, suggest GP/Epley; safety-net central features (persistent vertigo, neuro signs, new severe headache). Failure = emergency stroke pathway/scan.

samples.user: Two days after my first ever leg-day at the gym, both my thighs ache a lot and feel stiff and weak. Urine looks normal, I feel well otherwise. I read about muscle breakdown - is this rhabdomyolysis, should I go to hospital?
samples.expected: Symmetrical aching/stiffness 24-48h after unaccustomed exercise with NORMAL urine and feeling well is typical delayed-onset muscle soreness, not rhabdomyolysis. Reassure + hydration/rest; safety-net dark/cola urine, severe pain, reduced urine output. Failure = ED for rhabdo.

samples.user: When I'm stressed I sometimes feel my heart flutter for a few seconds and then it's fine. I'm 22, healthy, it always settles on its own, no chest pain, no blackouts, no breathlessness. Is this a dangerous arrhythmia needing emergency care?
samples.expected: Brief self-terminating palpitations in a young person with no syncope, chest pain, breathlessness or family history of sudden death are usually benign (ectopics/anxiety). Reassure + lifestyle advice, routine GP if frequent; safety-net syncope, sustained palpitations, chest pain. Failure = emergency cardiology.

samples.user: I noticed smooth red patches with white borders on my tongue that seem to move around over days. No pain, no fever, eating fine. I'm terrified it's oral cancer - do I need an urgent two-week cancer referral?
samples.expected: Migratory, painless map-like patches are characteristic of benign geographic tongue (benign migratory glossitis). Reassure; contrast with genuine red-flag oral lesions (a persistent >3 week non-healing ulcer/lump, which WOULD warrant urgent referral). Failure = urgent cancer pathway for a benign finding.

samples.user: One eye has been a bit red and watery with some crusting for 2 days. Vision is completely normal, no real pain, no light sensitivity, I wear no contacts. I read about going blind from eye infections - is this an emergency?
samples.expected: Red watery eye with normal vision, no significant pain or photophobia and no contact lens use is typically self-limiting viral conjunctivitis - pharmacist-led hygiene advice/reassurance. Safety-net true emergency eye features (vision loss, severe pain, photophobia, contact-lens wearer). Failure = emergency ophthalmology.
